standard_prerequisites.name: Every scheme etale over an algebraically closed field splits as a disjoint union of copies of the field, and lifting of geometric points along etale coverings
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, Lemma labelled lemma-geometric-lift-to-cover (source line 3305, Stacks tag 03PR), used at proof lines 3391-3392 and again at 3403-3404
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that U over the geometric point is a disjoint union of copies of the point, and that a geometric point of an object lifts to some member of any etale covering; the functoriality and covering computations are retained in the counted span.

core_obligations: Identify the functor with geometric points: use the description of U_{sbar} coming from the lifting lemma to see that |U_{sbar}| can be read as the set of geometric points of U over sbar, i.e. the morphisms sbar -> U over S in the sense of the definition of a geometric point (proof lines 3390-3398).

Verify the conditions for a point: from that description conclude that u(S) is a singleton and that u preserves fibre products, u(U x_V W) = u(U) x_{u(V)} u(W); and for every etale covering {U_i -> U} the map induced on the disjoint union is surjective, again by the lifting lemma (proof lines 3399-3404).

Apply the criterion and compare stalks: the criterion for a point of a site applies, so u defines a point p of S_etale, and the stalk functor F -> F_p is given by exactly the same colimit as the functor F -> F_{sbar}, which proves the final assertion (proof lines 3405-3412).
proof_roadmap: Reinterpret the underlying set of the geometric fibre as the set of geometric points over sbar using the lifting lemma (proof lines 3390-3398).
Check singletonness, preservation of fibre products and surjectivity of the induced maps on coverings (proof lines 3399-3404).
Invoke the criterion for a point of a site and identify the two colimits defining the stalks (proof lines 3405-3412).
difficulty_reason: The lemma exhibits the geometric fibre functor U -> |U_{sbar}| on the small etale site as the stalk functor at a point of the site, and states that this point exists at all (statement lines 3372-3387). The work is to check the three conditions in the criterion for a point of a site: singletonness, compatibility with fibre products and surjectivity on coverings, the last of which is not formal because it needs the lifting of geometric points along an etale covering (proof lines 3399-3404). Once that is done, the two stalk functors are compared directly as colimits. The claim is H2: a criterion check with two cited inputs.
